resources.string: The most famous sight of the Szalajka Valley, a stepped travertine waterfall.
A stalactite cave in Lillafüred, one of the most famous accessible caves of the Bükk.
A lookout point on the Bükk Plateau, with panorama to the southern edge and valleys.
One of the highest peaks of the Bükk, offering spectacular views of the mountains.
A bare limestone mountain above Bélapátfalva, with traces of former mining and panoramic views.
The most popular hiking valley of the Bükk, with springs, lakes and the Fátyol Waterfall.
A cave famous for its prehistoric site, with archaeological finds and strict protection.
A strictly protected cave with archaeological finds, part of an educational trail.
The longest valley of the Bükk, with caves, springs and hiking trails.
A castle ruin with scenic views of the surrounding mountains, also part of the National Blue Trail.
Beehive rocks with mysterious niches, unique archaeological formations.
A calm fishing and hiking lake surrounded by forests.
Prehistoric cave and distinctive rock tower, important archaeological site.
Unique niche rock formations, one of the most famous beehive rock areas in the Bükk.
A wonderful village in the Bükkalja region, known for its charming streets, wine cellars, and natural attractions.
A high-lying 800m tall plateau and spacious meadow on the Bükk Plateau, popular for hiking and relaxation.
The highest peaks of the Bükk (961m), offering breathtaking panoramic views of the surrounding landscape.
The highest peak of the Mátra and Hungary (1014 m), offering beautiful panoramic views and a lookout tower.
The second highest peak of the Mátra, known for its lookout tower and hiking trails.
The romantic Ilona Valley, home to Hungary\'s highest natural waterfall.
Forest walks and steam Bene await visitors at Mátrafüred, the gateway to the mountains.
Built on a volcanic cone, the Sirok Castle ruins are one of the Mátra\'s most impressive historical sites.
A small cave that showcases the geology of the surrounding area.
A former mine pit turned into a tarn, with uniquely colored water and wild surroundings.
The highest situated lake of the Mátra, a popular hiking destination with a lookout and nature trail.
The wildest gorge of the Mátra, with rocky terrain and striking geological formations.
A spectacular rocky peak near Kékestető, offering breathtaking views.
From the Disznó-kő there is a beautiful view of the mountains north of the Mátra Mountains.
One of the iconic peaks of the Mátra, with castle ruins and picturesque views of the surrounding mountains.
A sandstone peak, about 392 meters high, with one side of a steep cliff (about 60–80 m high) and a very nice view of the surrounding hills, towards the Mátra and Bükk Mountains.
Medieval castle ruins above Salgótarján, offering stunning views over the Karancs–Medves landscape.
Castle ruins perched on basalt columns in a unique geological setting.
The highest peak of the region (729 m), with a lookout tower and wide panoramic views.
Basalt rock formation on the edge of the Medves Plateau with unique shapes.
A national shrine set in a picturesque valley, a pilgrimage site with nearby hiking trails.
Central Europe’s largest basalt plateau with famous viewpoints and geological treasures.
A nature reserve featuring volcanic rock formations and castle ruins.
A forested valley with streams, a peaceful spot for hiking and excursions in the Heves–Borsod Hills.
A tranquil lake near Hangony, popular for fishing and hiking.
Protected landscape with diverse wildlife, rare plant and animal species, and hiking trails.
Three prominent hill peaks in the Heves–Borsod Hills, with panoramic hiking trails and forested surroundings.

A six-kilometer nature trail starting on the shore of Lázbérc Lake, named after the strictly protected salamander. Other protected animal species can be observed during the quiet hike around the lake.
The most famous sight of Aggtelek National Park, a monumental dripstone cave with multiple entrances and hiking tours.
A less-known but spectacular cave near Aggtelek, with unique karst formations.
A small lake on the edge of Aggtelek, a charming hiking stop close to the cave entrance.
The uniquely colored tarn near Jósvafő, one of the most beautiful lakes of the region.
Medieval castle ruins above Szögliget, with a stunning view of the surrounding hills and valleys.
Picturesque valley near Jósvafő, with streams and educational trails, ideal for excursions.
A stunning valley with steep rock walls, one of the most beautiful hiking spots of the Slovak Karst.
A unique Árpád-era church with twin sanctuaries, a rare example of medieval architecture.
A Baroque-style castle on an island by the Bódva River, one of the most beautiful aristocratic residences in Northeast Hungary.
A former mining lake with unique colors and steep cliffs, popular for hiking and diving.
The ruins of a 14th-century Pauline monastery in Szalonna Mountains, set in a charming forest environment.
A scenic lake in a former stone quarry, with dramatic cliffs and an educational trail.
A monumental statue of Christ above Tarcal, offering breathtaking views of the wine region.
The famous Rákóczi Castle, a key historical landmark in Sárospatak.
Impressive castle ruins on a hilltop, with one of the most beautiful panoramas of Zemplén.
A steep rocky ridge with views reaching as far as the Tatra Mountains on clear days.
The highest peak of Zemplén (895 m), with views stretching across the border.
One of Hungary’s most beautifully situated castles, restored with exhibitions and scenic views.
A smaller peak next to Nagy-Milic, accessible by forest hiking trails.
A spectacular suspension bridge and adventure park on Szár-hegy, with panoramic viewpoints.
Spectacular medieval castle ruins in the heart of the Zemplén, offering stunning views of the surrounding landscape.
Approaching only by boats, a scenic boardwalk along Lake Tisza, offering close views of aquatic habitats. It starts from Szabics port.
An educational trail showcasing the habitats and lookout points of Lake Tisza.
A modern visitor center with an aquarium and lookout tower at the gateway to Lake Tisza.
A wildlife park presenting native Hungarian animal species in the heart of Hortobágy.
The largest fishpond system of Hortobágy, an important bird habitat and hiking destination.
A family-friendly park showcasing traditional domestic animals of the Hortobágy.
A paradise for birdwatchers in the Tiszavalk Basin, with unique aquatic habitats.
The Hortobágy Starry Sky Park is Hungary\'s first international dark sky park, offering crystal-clear views of the Milky Way and the wonders of the night sky.
A thematic adventure park with labyrinths and interactive games, popular with families.
A fairy-tale Neo-Renaissance mansion, one of the most beautiful aristocratic buildings of the Hungarian Great Plain.
A national memorial site presenting the history of the Hungarian conquest and nation.
The largest arboretum in Hungary, rich in plant species and walking paths.
An interactive exhibition and wildlife park within the Körös-Maros National Park.
A renovated Baroque mansion offering historical exhibitions and cultural programs.
A sandy riverside beach at the Körös estuary, a popular summer destination.
A canopy walkway with a lookout tower, exploring the floodplain forests of the Maros River.
A historical theme park showcasing the different eras of Hungarian history.

A nature trail showcasing the rich birdlife of Fehér-tó (White Lake), including the local gull colony. The autumn crane migration, when tens of thousands of birds roost in the reeds, offers an outstanding spectacle.
A unique hand-shaped lookout tower near Hollókő with stunning views of the countryside.
Part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site, this medieval castle is Hollókő’s main attraction.
Special rhyolite tuff formations, unique natural treasures of Hungary.
A modern lookout tower near Alsópetény offering great panoramic views of the Cserhát hills.
Romantic castle ruins near Buják, a favorite destination for hikers.
A natural cave near Kishartyán, one of Palócföld’s hidden gems.
One of the world’s largest indoor Buddha statues, a spiritual center in Tar.
A historic lookout tower near Buják with beautiful panoramic views.
A steep gorge and rock crevice near Mátraverebély, surrounded by legends.
World-famous, 7-million-year-old petrified pine tree remains near Bükkábrány. The Ipolytarnóc Fossils Nature Reserve, the “Hungarian Jurassic Park”
A panoramic lookout tower on Tepke Hill with beautiful views of the Cserhát region.
A picturesque lake formed by mining near Apc, at the foot of the Mátra.
Medieval castle ruins on top of Szanda Hill, offering impressive views of the area.
Romantic castle ruins in the Cserhát hills, a popular destination for hikers.
Spectacular andesite columns near Szanda, unique geological formations.
Gyadai Meadow is a magical clearing at the foot of Naszály, with an educational trail and suspension bridges, perfect for family trips.
The Vácrátót National Botanical Garden is famous for its unique plant life.
Historic castle ruins above the village of Nógrád with a scenic panorama.
The Gyadai Educational Trail offers an exciting forest route presenting the wildlife of the Gyadai Meadow area.
Hegyes-tető is one of the most beautiful viewpoints of the Danube Bend, home to the Julianus Lookout.
The Julianus Lookout on Hegyes-tető offers a stunning view of the Danube Bend.
Csóványos is the highest peak of the Börzsöny, with a lookout tower offering a panoramic view.
Nagy-Hideg Hill is a popular hiking destination with a tourist house and winter sports opportunities.
The Remete Cave in the Pilis is a unique rock chamber with historical significance.
The Csarna Valley is a wild and secluded forest, one of the most untouched areas of the Börzsöny.
The Esztergom Basilica is Hungary\'s largest church, an imposing architectural landmark.
The Gömbölyű Rock stands out with its unusual shape among the landscape.
Királyrét is one of the most popular hiking areas in the Börzsöny, with a forest railway, small lake, and family-friendly trails.
The ruins of Drégely Castle offer stunning views of the Börzsöny and represent an important historical fortress.
The Saint Stephen Church in Nagybörzsöny is located in the historic center of the village and is a prominent landmark due to its architectural significance.
Zálog Peak is a scenic viewpoint in the Börzsöny Mountains near Nagybörzsöny, ideal for short hikes.
Hangyás Peak, located near Perőcsény, offers panoramic views of the Börzsöny Mountains.
Nagy-Koppány is a striking summit in the Börzsöny near Nagybörzsöny, popular among hikers.
Nagy-Sas Peak is a prominent summit of the Börzsöny Mountains near Nagybörzsöny, offering stunning panoramic views.
The Spartacus Trail in the Visegrád Hills offers stunning views of the Danube Bend. A popular hiking route.
The Apátkúti Valley near Visegrád is a favorite hiking spot with streams and shady forest trails.
Prédikálószék is one of the most famous viewpoints of the Danube Bend, offering a stunning panorama of the river.
The Vadálló Rocks rise near Prédikálószék with unique shapes and breathtaking views.
Rám Gorge is a wild and adventurous canyon with ladders and bridges along the trail.
Dömörkapu near Szentendre is a narrow valley and hiking spot in the Visegrád Mountains.
Sikárosi Meadow near Pomáz is a pleasant resting and hiking area along local trails.
Bertényi Miklós Botanical Garden in Visegrád features plant collections with walking paths and educational trails.
Borjúfő near Visegrád is a peak and viewpoint overlooking the Danube and surrounding hills.
Visegrád Citadel is a historic castle ruin in the Danube Bend with stunning panoramic views.
Kisoroszi Szigetcsúcs is a high viewpoint near Kisoroszi along the Danube.
Holdvilág-árok near Pomáz is a scenic rocky valley in the Pilis Mountains.
Anna Valley Waterfall near Szentendre is a charming hiking destination in the Pilis.
Pilisszentlászló Hegytető near Szentendre is a panoramic peak in the Pilis.
Dobogókő is the most famous peak of the Pilis, popular among hikers.
Rezső Lookout near Dömös offers excellent views of the Danube Bend.
Rám-hegy near Dömös is a rocky peak with views over the Danube Bend.
Hunyadi Meadow near Visegrád is a pleasant hiking and resting spot in the Pilis Mountains.
Hirsch Peak near Pilismarót is a panoramic summit in the Visegrád Mountains.
Fehér Rock near Esztergom is a popular hiking destination in the Danube Bend.
Vaskapu near Esztergom is a rocky gorge and hiking spot in the Danube Bend.
The Vasas Gorge near Szentendre is one of the most spectacular gorges of the Visegrád Mountains, featuring rocky walls and a wild, scenic landscape.
The Egri Castle replica near Pilisborosjenő is a popular hiking spot and film location.
Pilis-tető, at 756 meters, is the highest peak of the Pilis Mountains.
The Boldog Özséb Lookout on Pilis-tető offers breathtaking views of the Danube Bend.
Oszoly Peak rises above Csobánka with magnificent views of the region.
The Chapel of Our Lady in Zalaegerszeg stands in a picturesque hilltop setting.
Sas Rock near Pilisvörösvár is a striking rock formation and a popular hiking spot.
Leány Cave is a karst cave located near Esztergom.
Legény Cave opens in the hillside near Esztergom, next to Leány Cave.
The Dera Gorge at Pilisszentkereszt features unique rock walls and a stream bed. Family-friendly short walk.
The Camel Rock near Pilisborosjenő is a rock formation resembling a camel.
Róka-hegy Cave is a popular excursion site in District III.
The Jági trail near Pilisszentiván showcases the flora and fauna of the meadow and stream.
Sas Hill is a protected nature reserve in Budapest with panoramic city views.
Ördög-orom is a rocky outcrop at the edge of Budapest, popular with hikers.
Mátyás Hill is part of Óbuda’s hills, known for caves and trails.
Apáthy Rock offers one of the most beautiful views over Budapest.
Gellért Hill is a landmark of Budapest with historic sites and vistas.
The Garden of Philosophers is a peaceful park overlooking Buda.
Nyakas Rock in Biatorbágy is a striking natural formation and hiking spot.
The Tomb of Gül Baba is a historic site in Budapest.
Széchenyi Hill is a wooded area with a station of the Children’s Railway.
Hűvösvölgy is a popular hiking area in northern Budapest.
Normafa is one of Budapest’s most famous excursion spots.
The Lower Jegenye Valley with its stream and waterfall is a favorite trail in Solymár.
Solymár Castle ruins date back to the Middle Ages in the Buda Hills.
Árpád Lookout stands on Hármashatár Hill with panoramic views.
Remete Gorge is a wild ravine in District II.
János Hill is the highest point of Budapest, home to Erzsébet Lookout.
Great Hárs Hill is a beloved hiking destination in the Buda Hills.
Tündér Rock is an impressive rock formation near János Hill.
Farkas Hill near Budaörs is a popular hiking spot, there is a very nice view of the Törökugrató and the Budaörs Kopárok.
Cozy resting place along hiking trails near Páty.
Beautiful valley near Budakeszi, ideal for hiking and nature walks.
Arboretum with rich plant life in Budakeszi, featuring paths and a nature trail.
High point near Nagykovácsi, with panoramic views of the Buda Hills.
Rocky hill near Solymár, a popular hiking spot.
Lookout near Nagykovácsi, offering fantastic views of the Buda Hills.
The highest point of Budapest, Nagy-Kopasz, stands at 559 meters, offering fantastic panoramic views.
Bokodi Lake near Oroszlány, ideal for fishing and relaxation.
Historic church in Zsámbék, known for its medieval origins and architecture.
Kamalduli monastery in Tata surrounded by forests, calm environment and cultural value.
Tatai Fényes Nature Trail, forest path with spring and educational signs.
Öreg-kő, distinctive rock formation near Bajót.
Jankovich Cave, an interesting cave tour near Bajót.
The highest peak of Gerecse (634m), with panoramic views.
Turul Monument in Tatabánya, historical and panoramic site.
Szelim Cave, impressive karst cave in Tatabánya.
Öreg Lake in Tata, a place for relaxation and hiking.
Peskő Cave in Vértestolna, popular hiking cave.
Bánya Hill near Tardos, suitable for hiking and views.
The Tardos Canopy Trail near Süttő is a unique walkway through the treetops, offering stunning views of the Gerecse forests.
Located on the slopes of the Gerecse above Héreg, the arched Király Spring offers a charming forest clearing, a well-equipped resting area, and a large shelter for hikers.
Pogány-kő, a scenic rocky peak in Pákozd in the Velence Hills.
Bella Lake, a peaceful lake in Pákozd, perfect for hiking.
Likaskő, a characteristic rock formation in Sukoró in the Velence Hills.
Bodza Valley, a forested valley in Pákozd, part of a hiking trail.
Nagy-legelő, a wide meadow in Sukoró, ideal for excursions.
Meleg-hegy, the highest peak of the Velence Hills (352m), a panoramic hilltop in Sukoró.
Kőkapu Valley, a forested valley with a stream near Csákberény, ideal for hiking.
Varga Hill, a scenic peak near Csákberény, a notable point in the Vértes Hills.
Bauxite Mine Lookout, a former mining area with a viewing point in Csákvár.
Mária Gorge, steep canyon near Tatabánya, part of a hiking trail.
Vitány Castle, medieval castle near Tatabánya, historical landmark.
Vértes Panorama Trail, nature and scenic trail near Csákberény.
Csókakő Castle, medieval ruins in Csókakő, popular among hikers.
Kőris Hill, at 709 meters, is the highest peak of the Bakony Mountains, offering stunning views over the forested landscape and the Pannonhalma Hills.
The Hubertlaki Lake, also known as the “Bakony Dead Lake,” is a magical forest lake made unique by the trunks of submerged trees rising from its surface.
The Cuha Valley is a spectacular gorge where the stream runs alongside railway viaducts and rocky cliffs through the forest.
The Kőmosó Gorge near Csesznek features steep rock walls and small waterfalls, making it a favorite hiking spot.
The Római Bath near Bakonynána is one of the most beautiful natural attractions of the Bakony, with the Gaja Stream’s waterfalls and rocky canyon.
The Castle of Csesznek is an iconic fortress of the Bakony, offering stunning panoramic views of the surrounding hills and valleys.
The Zirc Arboretum is a botanical garden in the heart of the Bakony, home to rare plant species and towering trees.
The Zirc Cistercian Abbey is the symbol of the Bakony’s main town, with its Baroque church and impressive monastic buildings.
The Kerteskő Gorge is a deep, wild valley near Bakonybél, where a small stream winds between steep rock walls.
The Úrkút Paleokarst is a unique geological site where ancient seabed limestone layers and caves are exposed.
Thury Castle stands in the center of Várpalota; once a frontier fortress of Transdanubia, today it serves as a museum and cultural center.
The ruins of Bátorkő Castle, one of the oldest stone fortresses in the Bakony, rise on a forested hill near Várpalota.
The ruins of Essegvár stand near Bánd, offering a beautiful view over the valleys and ridges of the Bakony Mountains.
The Károlyi Castle in Fehérvárcsurgó is an impressive neoclassical mansion, now serving as a cultural and event venue.
The Nádasdy Castle in Nádasdladány was built in a romantic neo-Gothic style and is one of Hungary’s most beautiful castles.
Fajdas Hill rises near Várpalota, offering scenic forested slopes and wide views over the eastern Bakony region.
The Burok Valley is one of Hungary’s most untouched forest canyons, rich in lush vegetation and hidden streambeds.
The Károlyi Lookout in Bodajk rises above the Gaja Gorge, offering a stunning panorama over the southern Bakony and the Mór Valley.
The chapel above Magyarpolány stands on a hilltop as an iconic pilgrimage site, offering beautiful views of the village and the gentle hills of the Bakony.
The Caveman’s Cave near Magyarpolány is part of the Sacred Trail, where nature and history meet in a unique harmony.
The Odvaskő Cave near Bakonyszücs is one of the most famous karst caves of the Bakony Mountains, easily accessible via a nature trail and admired for its unique rock formations.
Szarvaskő Castle towers above Döbrönte as one of the most romantic castles in the Bakony, offering beautiful views over the nearby valleys and woodlands.
The Széchenyi Zsigmond Lookout near Tés provides an excellent panorama of the Bakony’s forested landscape, and on clear days you can even see Lake Balaton.
The Veszprém Valley, also known as Fejes Valley, is the green heart of the city — a peaceful place of walking paths, streams, and shade at the foot of the Bakony.

The Fehér-kövek (“White Rocks”) near Sümeg offer stunning views over the town and its famous castle. From the top of these striking formations, the western edge of the Bakony Mountains unfolds in all its beauty.
The ruins of Hegyesd Castle stand atop one of the most scenic witness hills of the Tapolca Basin, offering a stunning view over the basalt peaks and rolling hills of the Balaton Uplands.
From the Somlyó Hill lookout, there is a breathtaking panorama of the eastern basin of Lake Balaton and the Tihany Peninsula.
One of Lake Balaton’s most famous castles, offering stunning views of the lake and the surrounding volcanic hills.
From the Eötvös Károly Lookout in Köveskál, visitors can admire the scenic panorama of the Káli Basin and Lake Balaton.
The Koloska Valley near Balatonfüred is a popular hiking destination with a stream and shady forest paths.
The impressive rock formations of Koloska are popular with hikers and nature photographers alike.
The ruins of Csobánc Castle offer one of the most beautiful panoramic views of the Balaton Uplands, especially at sunset.
The basalt columns of Hegyestű are striking reminders of the region’s volcanic past, offering a sweeping view of the Balaton Uplands.
One of the highest points of the Tihany Peninsula, offering a spectacular view over the land and Lake Balaton.
The iconic witness hill of the Balaton Uplands, famous for its wines and breathtaking scenery.
From the Páholykő viewpoint, visitors can enjoy a wide panorama over Lake Balaton and Badacsony Hill.
The Egry József viewpoint offers the same stunning scenery that inspired the painter’s Balaton landscapes.
From the Tördemic Lookout, you can enjoy a fine view of the Badacsony slopes and the nearby volcanic hills.
The Folly Arboretum enchants visitors with its unique conifer collection and panoramic terraces.
The top of Tóti Hill offers the most spectacular panoramic view of the Balaton Uplands.
The Salföld Pauline monastery ruins preserve the memory of medieval monastic life in a picturesque setting.
St. George Hill is famous for its basalt organ formations, vineyards, and superb views over Lake Balaton.
The Jókai Lookout on Tamás Hill in Balatonfüred offers sweeping views over the town and the eastern basin of the lake.
Recsek Hill is a quiet hiking spot with fine views of the wooded Balaton Uplands.
Nyereg Hill is one of Tihany’s most scenic points, lying between the Inner and Outer Lakes.
From Apáti Hill, you can see the unique landscape of the Tihany Peninsula and both of its lakes.
The Hálóeresztő rock at southern Tihany offers a tranquil panoramic view over Lake Balaton.
Csúcs Hill, one of the highest points on the Tihany Peninsula, offers great views and unique basalt formations.
The Stone Sea at Szentbékkálla is one of the Balaton Uplands’ most striking geological wonders, with massive rock formations.
The “Queen’s Skirt” basalt cone near Szigliget Castle can also be admired from the Óvári lookout point.
The “Beautiful Lookout” truly lives up to its name, with a magnificent view over Lake Balaton and St. George Hill.

Rising above Zalaszántó, Tátika Castle is one of the oldest stone fortresses of the Balaton Uplands. It is surrounded by a sacred ancient beech forest that gives the site a mystical and tranquil atmosphere where nature and history meet.
Pad-kő lookout near Balatongyörök offers a breathtaking view of Lake Balaton and the surrounding hills.
From the Batsányi Lookout above Balatongyörök, you can enjoy a stunning panorama of the Keszthely Bay and the witness hills of the Tapolca Basin.
The Garga Hill near Balatongyörök features a lookout tower with a splendid view of the western basin of Lake Balaton.
The Festetics Lookout in Gyenesdiás offers wonderful views of Lake Balaton, the Keszthely Hills, and the Tapolca Basin.
The Büdöskút Rest House is a popular stop in the Keszthely Hills, where forest trails meet, offering hikers a peaceful place to rest amid nature.
Varsás Hill rises above Gyenesdiás, a pleasant hiking destination offering a beautiful view of the surrounding hills and Lake Balaton.
Nagymező is one of the most beautiful meadows in the Keszthely Hills, an ideal spot for picnics and relaxation for nature lovers.
Köves-tető is the highest peak of the Keszthely Hills at 444 meters above sea level, offering a stunning panorama of Lake Balaton and the surrounding landscape.
Csóka-kő, near Cserszegtomaj, offers a wonderful panorama over the Keszthely Hills and the Balaton region.
The Zalaszántó Stupa is the largest Buddhist monument in Central Europe, a symbol of peace and tranquility nestled in the quiet hills.
Kő-orra is a striking rock formation near Várvölgy in the Keszthely Hills, offering a beautiful view of the surrounding hills and valleys.
The Vadludak Camping in Lipót is a popular retreat in the heart of Szigetköz, ideal for canoeists and nature lovers.
The Denkpál fish ladder is a unique structure on the Danube that allows fish to migrate freely and is a popular excursion spot near Dunasziget.
Héderváry Castle in Hédervár is an impressive historic building set in a beautiful park with rich heritage.
The Trianon sluice in Rajka is a popular starting point for canoe tours exploring the waterways of Szigetköz.
Vadvíz Camping near Dunakiliti is a favored base for canoe tours and family camping in the heart of Szigetköz.
Kisvesszősi Camping near Cikolasziget is a popular canoe launch site and rest spot for nature enthusiasts.
The Dunasziget kayak and canoe launch is an ideal starting point for exploring Szigetköz’s waterways.
The Fairy Island Ecopark near Dunasziget offers a nature-friendly campsite with family programs and water-tour options.
Dodó Wildlife Farm and Fishing Lake in Dunaremete offers family-friendly recreation with a restaurant, petting zoo, and fishing opportunities.
The Pókmacskási Island lies near Ásványráró among the Danube’s side branches. Its tranquil, natural surroundings make it ideal for birdwatching and canoe trips.

Morotva Lake, located near Dunaszeg, is a popular spot for fishing and hiking thanks to its calm waters and natural surroundings. The Morotva Lake educational trail runs alongside, offering insight into the local wildlife.
Part Camping Ásványráró, located in the heart of Szigetköz, is ideal for relaxation and also serves as a starting point for canoe trips.
The Halrekesztő Lock near Ásványráró is an important water engineering structure on the Danube, playing a role in water regulation and fish migration.
The Farkaslyuki Lock near Ásványráró is a key part of the Szigetköz water system, ensuring controlled flow through the Danube’s side branches.
The Bolgányi Bridge at Kunsziget spans the Danube, holding historical and strategic significance, and is popular among local cyclists and hikers.
Károly Hill in Sopron features a lookout providing stunning panoramic views of the city and surrounding area.
Szalamandra Lake near Sopron offers a peaceful setting ideal for fishing and nature walks.
Várhely Peak near Sopron has a lookout with wide panoramic views of the surrounding landscape.
Fáber Meadow in Felsőlövérek is an open area perfect for picnics and walks.
Magas-bérc near Sopron is the highest point in Hungary’s Sopron Mountains (557 m) and a must-visit for hikers.
The Erdő Háza Ecotourism Visitor Center offers insight into the wildlife of Sopron’s forests and provides eco-friendly programs.
Lővér Adventure Park in Felsőlövérek offers outdoor adventure activities for families and young people.
Tolvaj-árok is a gorge near Sopron, popular among hikers and nature enthusiasts.
The Cserkész Chapel in Sopronbánfalva is a small church with historical and religious significance.
Taródi Castle in Felsőlövérek is a unique architectural gem open to visitors in Sopron.
The Car Rest Area in the Brennberg Valley features picnic spots, a fire pit, and a playground, ideal for families.
Írott-kő is Hungary’s westernmost and highest point (883 m), offering stunning views from its lookout and serving as a starting point of the Blue Trail.
The Jurisics Castle is Kőszeg’s symbol, known for its heroic defense during the 16th-century Ottoman siege; today it functions as a museum and cultural center.
Kopasz-Kendig is one of the scenic peaks of the Kőszeg Mountains, a popular hiking spot with beautiful forest views.
Óház Hill is a favorite hiking destination in the Kőszeg Mountains, featuring a lookout with panoramic views over the town and hills.
The Hörmann Spring near Velem provides fresh drinking water and serves as a refreshing rest spot for hikers.
The Seven Springs near Kőszeg are a symbol of patriotism and a popular pilgrimage and hiking site in the region.
Calvary Hill in Kőszeg features stations of the cross and a chapel, offering both spiritual significance and scenic views over the town.
Lockenhaus Castle in Burgenland, Austria, is a medieval fortress now serving as a museum and cultural center, famous for its legends of the Knights Templar.
The Rechnitz Bathing Lake (Badesee Rechnitz) just across the border is a popular summer destination with clean water and a well-maintained beach area.
The Cák Wine Cellar Row near Kőszeg is an ethnographic museum where traditional wine cellars showcase the region’s rich viticultural and rural heritage.
Lake Hársas near Szentgotthárd is a popular bathing lake with a tidy beach, forest trails, and peaceful natural surroundings.
The Rába riverside dock near Csákánydoroszló is a popular starting point for canoe trips along the scenic Rába River.
Güssing Castle, also known as the Batthyány Castle, is one of the oldest fortresses in Burgenland, now a museum showcasing the history of the Batthyány family.
The Pottery House in Magyarszombatfa preserves the Őrség region’s traditional pottery craftsmanship, offering insight into local folk art and ceramics.
Katalin Hill near Kétvölgy features a lookout tower offering stunning panoramic views of the rolling hills of the Őrség and neighboring Slovenia.
Pityerszer in Szalafő is home to the Őrség Open-Air Museum, preserving authentic peasant houses and traditional rural life of the region.
The Holy Trinity Church of Velemér is a 13th-century monument known for its medieval frescoes and the way sunlight illuminates its sacred interior.
Lake Vadása near Hegyhátszentjakab is a beloved recreational spot with clear waters, surrounded by forests and hiking trails.
The Skirted Belfry of Pankasz is a unique wooden structure and a symbol of the Őrség region’s traditional architecture.
The European Bison Hide in Szalafő is a unique attraction of the Őrség National Park, offering visitors a chance to observe bison and other wildlife in their natural habitat.
The Triple Border Stone (Hármashatárkő) is the highest point of the Őrség region at 387 m, marking the meeting point of Hungary, Slovenia, and Austria—a unique geographical and hiking landmark.
The artillery bunker near Iklódbördőce is a World War II relic, a reminder of the region’s military past, accessible along a forest trail.
The lookout on Új Hill near Pusztaszentlászló offers a beautiful panoramic view over the rolling Zala hills and nearby villages.
The Göcsej Village Museum in Zalaegerszeg is Hungary’s first open-air ethnographic museum, showcasing traditional rural life and architecture of the Göcsej region.
The Egervár Castle is a Renaissance-style monument once owned by the Nádasdy family, now serving as a cultural and tourist attraction.
Tukora Hill near Újudvar offers scenic views over the Zala Hills and is a favorite destination for hikers and nature lovers.
The Kőszikla Gorge near Újudvar features dramatic rock walls and springs along a picturesque forest trail.
The Kalocsay Kálmán (Esperanto) Spring in Nagybakónak is a popular spot named after the famous doctor and poet, surrounded by tranquil forest paths.
The TV Tower in Zalaegerszeg is one of the city’s landmarks. Its observation deck offers panoramic views over the city and the surrounding hills, with a café at its base.
The Vétyem Forest Reserve, also known as the Vétyem Beech Forest, is one of Zala’s most pristine natural areas, home to untouched beech woods and rare plant species.
The Szécsisziget Buffalo Reserve is part of the Mura region’s protected area, where visitors can observe Hungarian water buffalo living in their natural environment.
The Budafa Arboretum covers more than 100 hectares and features diverse plant species and shaded trails, making it a popular nature destination in the Letenye Hills.
The highest point of the Zala Hills, peaking at 338 meters. It is a popular destination for gentle hiking trails winding through the diverse Zala forests.

A nature trail winding through the Zalakaros Park Forest, interactively showcasing the local fungi, forest animals, and birds, whose songs can be heard on sound boards. Unique wave-shaped benches provide resting spots along the route.

The Zselic Star Park is the center of Hungary’s first International Dark Sky Park. Visitors can explore the wonders of the night sky through telescope demonstrations, planetarium shows, and interactive exhibits in the heart of the light pollution-free Zselic region.
Hidden deep in the Zselic forests, Lake Ropolyi is a popular spot for hikers and nature lovers. The area offers a scenic trail, picnic areas, and a diverse range of wildlife.

Szigetvár Castle is one of Hungary’s most important historical sites, where Miklós Zrínyi and his defenders fought heroically against the Ottoman army in 1566. Today it serves as a museum, memorial, and venue for cultural events.

The Bükkösd Eco Park showcases the natural and cultural treasures of Southern Transdanubia. Visitors can learn about sustainable living and local wildlife through interactive exhibits and nature trails.
Katica Tanya is a family adventure park and eco-farm where children can meet farm animals, enjoy playgrounds and slides, and experience the everyday life of the countryside.
The Hollófészek is the highest point of Zselic, 358 m. The lookout offers a stunning panorama of the surrounding forests and valleys, and in clear weather you can even see the Mecsek ranges.
The most significant dripstone cave in the Mecsek, whose stream originates from a lake at the entrance. It\'s recommended as a therapeutic cave for asthma and allergy sufferers.
An easily accessible elevation offering a beautiful view of the Orfű Lakes and the Western Mecsek range. It serves as a perfect resting spot.
A popular resting spot located above Pécs, providing a magnificent panorama of the city and its surroundings. Ideal for watching sunsets.
The highest peak of the Mecsek (682 m), a true challenge for forest hikers. The military radar station and lookout tower on its top dominate the landscape from afar.
One of the most romantic valleys in the Eastern Mecsek, featuring small streams, cascades, and wild, picturesque scenery. A favorite destination for hikers.
A medieval castle located in the Eastern Mecsek, whose ruins offer an exciting glimpse into Hungarian history. Often hosts historical events.
A rare attraction of the Mecsek. The waterfall trickles down small rocks, best visited during rainy seasons when the water flow is abundant.
A protected natural area characterized by steep cliffs, cool springs, and a charming stream. The valley\'s biological diversity is exceptional.
A deeply incised, rugged valley located next to the Melegmányi Valley. Perfectly suited for quiet, forest walks.
Distinctive and peculiar rock formations of the Mecsek. Legends speak of the stones once depicting people who were turned into stone.
A rock crest that offers breathtaking views. On clear days, you can see far from the steep edge. An iconic spot in the Western Mecsek.
A beautiful, gentle landscape with meadows and forest patches, showcasing the more rolling side of the Eastern Mecsek. Ideal for leisurely walks and picnics.

The Stone-Crusher Giant is a large wooden sculpture carved from acacia wood by artist Gábor Baráth, it is part of the Mecsek Giants Adventure Trail. According to local legend, the Stone-Crusher was one of the mountain giants who could crush rocks with his bare hands. Blending art with nature, the sculpture offers a playful, fairy-tale atmosphere — visitors can even climb onto it — making it a popular hiking and photo spot in the heart of the Mecsek.
Often called the "Switzerland of the Eastern Mecsek," where the stream creates small waterfalls and cascades. One of the region\'s most beautiful hiking spots.
A special waterfall near Kisújbánya that slides diagonally over the rocks. It is most spectacular during rainy periods.
A hilltop rising above Komló, offering a good panorama of other peaks of the Eastern Mecsek and the surrounding settlements on clear days.
It rises above the Orfű Lakes, with a lookout tower on its top providing a marvelous all-round view of the lake system and the forests of the Western Mecsek.
The highest point of the Western Mecsek (602 m), featuring the remains of an ancient earth fort and a Pauline monastery ruin on its summit. Its historical and natural significance is outstanding.
A hill above Harkány with a lookout point offering a panorama of the Dráva Plain and the Villány Hills ridge. An ideal resting spot while exploring the area\'s wine cellars.
An open-air sculpture exhibition located in the unique Nagyharsány Quarry, featuring works by international artists since the 1960s. A unique blend of industrial landscape and art.
Siklós\'s most important Ottoman-era monument, one of the best-preserved mosques in the country. It is situated near Siklós Castle.
An elevation near Kistótfalu, offering views over the rolling vineyards in the heart of the Villány wine region. A popular hiking and resting point.
A trail running along the northern slopes of Szársomlyó, showcasing the mountain\'s special Mediterranean flora, including the rare Butcher\'s-broom (csodabogyó).
The highest point of the Villány Hills (442 m). This highly protected nature reserve is home to many rare plant and animal species, including the Autumn Snowflake. Only guided tours are allowed.
One of Hungary\'s largest and most intact medieval castles. It played a significant role from King Matthias to the Ottoman conquest, now serving as a museum and event center.
